code: set.seed(1) n <- 400 X <- matrix(runif(n * 2, -1, 1), ncol = 2) A <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5) Y <- ifelse(X[, 1] >= 0, A, 0.5 * (1 - A)) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3)  common <- list(   propensity        = 0.5,   n_shuffles        = 10,   contextual_policy = "linear",   best_arm          = "simple",   reward_model      = "linear",   seed              = 0 ) r_kpe  <- do.call(kpe,        c(list(X = X, A = A, Y = Y), common)) r_trev <- do.call(train_eval, c(list(X = X, A = A, Y = Y), common)) r_papd <- do.call(papd,       c(list(X = X, A = A, Y = Y), common))  summary_row <- function(r) {   ci <- r$confidence_interval   data.frame(method  = r$method,              psi     = r$psi,              ci_lo   = ci[1],              ci_hi   = ci[2],              p_value = r$p_value) } do.call(rbind, lapply(list(r_kpe, r_trev, r_papd), summary_row)) ##       method       psi     ci_lo     ci_hi      p_value ## 1        kpe 0.1995672 0.1511233 0.2480111 4.053638e-15 ## 2 train_eval 0.2009647 0.1306704 0.2712589 3.469744e-08 ## 3       papd 0.1919487 0.1441637 0.2397337 1.651229e-14

title: User-supplied learners
text: See vignette("getting-started", package = "kpe") installation full learner/backend table. runnable example uses base-R learners ("linear", "simple") plus user-supplied reward object, needs extra packages. optional xgboost snippet near end requires xgboost package.

title: User-supplied learners
text: user-supplied learner must R list fit predict elements matching following signatures. list instance reused across folds, fit reset state needs training arguments — example via closure assigns parent environment <<-.
code: # Reward model list(   fit     = function(X, y) { ... ; invisible(NULL) },   predict = function(X) numeric_vector ) # X is an (n, d + 1) numeric matrix whose last column is the observed # action. predict returns a length-n numeric vector of predicted # outcomes.  # Contextual policy list(   fit     = function(X, A, Y, n_actions) { ... ; invisible(NULL) },   predict = function(X) integer_vector ) # predict returns a length-n integer vector of actions in # {0, ..., n_actions - 1}.  # Best-arm (non-contextual) list(   fit     = function(A, Y, propensities, n_actions) { ... ; invisible(NULL) },   predict = function() integer_scalar ) # predict returns a single integer action in {0, ..., n_actions - 1}.

title: User-supplied learners
text: learner records mean y fit time returns reward prediction predict time. statistical value; minimal object satisfies reward-model contract.
code: library(kpe) byo_reward <- local({   mu <- NULL   list(     fit     = function(X, y) { mu <<- mean(y); invisible(NULL) },     predict = function(X) rep(mu, nrow(as.matrix(X)))   ) })  set.seed(0) n <- 300 X <- matrix(runif(n * 2, -1, 1), ncol = 2) A <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5) Y <- ifelse(X[, 1] >= 0, A, 0.5 * (1 - A)) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3)  fit <- kpe(X, A, Y, propensity = 0.5,            n_shuffles = 4, n_folds = 6,            reward_model      = byo_reward,            contextual_policy = "linear",            best_arm          = "simple",            seed = 0) print(fit) ## K-Fold Personalization Estimator (kpe) ##   n_samples  = 300 ##   n_shuffles = 4, n_folds = 6 ##   psi        = 0.2586 (SE 0.03006) ##   95% CI    = [0.1997, 0.3175] ##   p-value    = 2.248e-16 (one-sided) ##   policy stability = 0.9933

title: User-supplied learners
text: regressor exposes fit(X, y) predict(X) can adapted assigning fitted state closure calling predict prediction time. snippet wraps xgboost::xgboost (hard dependency kpe; load separately required). construction applies user-supplied contextual_policy (providing fit(X, , Y, n_actions) predict(X) returning integer actions {0, ..., n_actions - 1}) user-supplied best_arm (providing fit(, Y, propensities, n_actions) predict() returning single integer action).
code: library(xgboost)  byo_xgb <- local({   model <- NULL   list(     fit = function(X, y) {       model <<- xgboost::xgboost(data = as.matrix(X), label = y,                                  nrounds = 50, verbose = 0)       invisible(NULL)     },     predict = function(X) {       as.numeric(stats::predict(model, as.matrix(X)))     }   ) })  fit <- kpe(X, A, Y, propensity = 0.5,            reward_model = byo_xgb, seed = 0)

title: JobCorps
code: library(kpe)  # One-hot every covariate column (mirrors the OneHotEncoder loop in the # Python JobCorps vignette), reading the same cleaned CSV. Produces: #   X                : one-hot encoded covariates #   A                : 0/1 treatment #   Y                : continuous earnings outcome #   age_group_index  : 1-based column indices of the AGEGROUP one-hots df <- read.csv(file.path(Sys.getenv("KPE_DATA_DIR"),                          "jobcorps_cleaned_nonan_full_with_offset.csv")) Y <- df$EARNY4 A <- as.integer(df$TREATMNT)  feature_columns <- setdiff(names(df), c("EARNY4", "TREATMNT")) encoded <- list() age_group_cols <- character(0) for (col in feature_columns) {   lv <- sort(unique(df[[col]]))            # sklearn OneHotEncoder sorts categories   mm <- outer(df[[col]], lv, `==`) + 0     # full one-hot, no reference level dropped   colnames(mm) <- paste0(col, "_", lv)   encoded[[col]] <- mm   if (col == "AGEGROUP") age_group_cols <- colnames(mm) } X <- do.call(cbind, encoded) X[is.na(X)] <- 0 age_group_index <- match(age_group_cols, colnames(X))   # 1-based indices  pa_x <- prop.table(table(A))[as.character(A)]

Choose m=m =n_nuisance_folds folds fit nuisances (default m=K−1m = K - 1); evaluation block size b=K−mb = K - m must divide KK, folds tile G=K/bG = K / b non-overlapping evaluation blocks. block gg: Fit nuisances — reward model m(x,)m(x, ), contextual policy π(x)\pi(x), best single arm π0\pi_0, (is_rct = FALSE) propensity p̂(∣x)\hat p(\mid x) — mm folds outside block gg. Evaluate AIPW influence function (Eq. S17) bb folds block gg: ψi=m(X,π(X))−m(X,π0)+𝟏{=π(X),π0≠π(X)}−𝟏{=π0,π0≠π(X)}p(∣X)(Y−m(X,)).\psi_i = m(X, \pi(X)) - m(X, \pi_0)         + \frac{\mathbf{1}\{= \pi(X), \pi_0 \neq \pi(X)\}               - \mathbf{1}\{= \pi_0, \pi_0 \neq \pi(X)\}}              {p(\mid X)}\,(Y - m(X, )). Concatenating per-block ψ\psi vectors across GG blocks yields length-nn vector sample evaluated exactly ; shuffle-level summary ψ̂s=mean\hat\psi_s = \text{mean} σ̂s=std\hat\sigma_s = \text{std}. Unlike original Algorithm 2 (Li Brunskill, Science 2026) — fits policy reward models disjoint subsets non-evaluation folds — kpe2 fits every nuisance mm folds. default m=K−1m = K - 1 gives b=1b = 1 G=KG = K: leave-one-fold-, fitting every nuisance K−1K - 1 folds evaluating remaining one, rotated KK times (K=6K = 6, 5/6 data fit 1/6 evaluate). is_rct = TRUE (default), p(∣X)p(\mid X) known design propensity nothing fit ; is_rct = FALSE, fitted p̂(∣x)\hat p(\mid x) used influence evaluation best-arm comparison.

title: Methods
text: Algorithm 2 repeated SS random shuffles, per-shuffle (ψ̂s,σ̂s)(\hat\psi_s, \hat\sigma_s) pairs aggregated via ψ̂=1S∑sψ̂s,Var̂(ψ̂)=1S∑s(σ̂s2+(ψ̂s−ψ̂)2)/n.\hat\psi = \tfrac{1}{S}\sum_s \hat\psi_s, \qquad \widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\hat\psi) = \tfrac{1}{S}\sum_s\!\left(\hat\sigma_s^2 + (\hat\psi_s - \hat\psi)^2\right)\!\Big/\,n. first term accounts within-shuffle influence variance; second term accounts across-shuffle variability introduced sample splitting. one-sided upper-tail t-statistic t=ψ̂/Var̂(ψ̂)t = \hat\psi / \sqrt{\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\hat\psi)}, reported p_value corresponding upper-tail probability tn−1t_{n-1}. confidence_interval 95% Wald interval ψ̂±1.96Var̂(ψ̂)\hat\psi \pm 1.96 \sqrt{\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\hat\psi)}.

text: Inputs. X: n × d numeric matrix data frame covariates. : length-n integer vector observed actions {0, ..., K-1} (factors coerced). Y: length-n numeric vector observed outcomes. propensity: scalar, length-n vector, n × K matrix giving p(| X) observed action; required is_rct=TRUE (default) ignored is_rct=FALSE (propensity fit nuisance folds). Additional arguments: n_shuffles, n_folds, n_nuisance_folds, is_rct, contextual_policy, best_arm, reward_model, propensity_model, policy_features, n_cores, seed, verbose. Output. S3 list class "kpe". Computation. K-Fold Personalization Estimator Li Brunskill (2026), kpe2 shared-nuisance variant: n_shuffles random partitions data n_folds folds, nuisances — reward model, contextual policy, best-arm learner, (is_rct=FALSE) propensity — fit shared set n_nuisance_folds folds, AIPW influence function evaluated held-block remaining n_folds - n_nuisance_folds folds. blocks tile folds without overlap, sample evaluated exactly per shuffle. default n_nuisance_folds = n_folds - 1 gives leave-one-fold-: n_folds = 6, every nuisance fit 5/6 data evaluated held-1/6, rotated six times. Algorithm-1 variance decomposition combines per-shuffle (psi_hat, sigma_hat) pairs point estimate, standard error, one-sided upper-tail t-test p-value, 95% Wald confidence interval.

code: set.seed(0) n <- 200 X <- matrix(runif(n * 3, -1, 1), ncol = 3) A <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5) Y <- ifelse(X[, 1] >= 0, A, 0.5 * (1 - A)) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3) fit <- kpe(X, A, Y, propensity = 0.5,            n_shuffles = 4, n_folds = 6,            contextual_policy = "linear",            best_arm = "simple",            reward_model = "linear",            seed = 0) print(fit) #> K-Fold Personalization Estimator (kpe) #>   n_samples  = 200 #>   n_shuffles = 4, n_folds = 6 #>   psi        = 0.2073 (SE 0.03445) #>   95% CI    = [0.1397, 0.2748] #>   p-value    = 4.199e-09 (one-sided) #>   policy stability = 0.97

title: kpe 0.1.0
text: Initial release. Point estimate, confidence interval, one-sided p-value personalization effect via two-fold K-Fold Personalization Estimator Li Brunskill (2026). Three estimators — kpe(), train_eval(), papd() — sharing one argument signature returning "kpe" S3 object print(), summary(), confint(), coef() methods. Pluggable reward, contextual-policy, best-arm learners via built-strings (backed ranger, policytree, grf, glmnet Suggests) user-supplied fit/predict objects. estimate reproducible regardless n_cores: per-shuffle fold split forest seeds pinned independent parallel backend.
